knitr::opts_chunk$set(
  collapse = TRUE,

knitr::read_chunk("example_fit.R")

```{r setup}
library(PEPI)
library(dplyr)
library(ggplot2)
library(ggpubr)
```

We fit PEPI on the polyclonal dataset generated in
`vignette("Data_generation")` and shipped with the package: a wild-type
population switching between the "-" and "+" epistates, in which a driver
(mutant `B`) is acquired by a "-" cell. Cells are sorted by epistate and
sequenced at two time points, and the population is counted at the same
times.

The parameters used to simulate the data are:

```{r}
truth = c(
  "lambda_n" = 1,
  "s_epi" = 0.5,
  "s_driver[1]" = 0.35,
  "omega_p_wt" = 8e-3,
  "tmrca" = 0,
  "t_driver[1]" = 4,
  "omega_p_driver[1]" = 4e-2,
  "omega_n_driver[1]" = 0.3
)
```

## The data

```{r}
data("forest")
data("muts")
```

The phylogenetic forest of the sampled cells, restricted to the branches of
50 random cells per sample, coloured by species (left), and with the driver
branch and the truncal node highlighted (right). Below, the pairwise and
marginal VAF spectra of the four sorted samples, with the same labels.

```{r, fig.width=12, fig.height=6.5}
set.seed(31)

ids_1 = (forest %>% filter(!is.na(sample), sample == "Sampling_1") %>%
  pull(cell_id))[sample(x = 1:3000, size = 50, replace = FALSE)]
ids_2 = (forest %>% filter(!is.na(sample), sample == "Sampling_2") %>%
  pull(cell_id))[sample(x = 1:3000, size = 50, replace = FALSE)]

all_ids = c(0)
for (id in c(ids_1, ids_2)){
  all_ids = unique(c(all_ids, get_branch(forest = forest, cell_id = id, stop_id = 0)))
}

forest_plot = forest %>% mutate(sample = gsub(x = sample, pattern = "Sampling_", replacement = "T"))

driver_id = forest %>% filter(mutant == "B") %>% pull(cell_id) %>% min()
branch_driver = get_branch(forest = forest, cell_id = driver_id, stop_id = 0)

muts_plot = muts %>%
  mutate(label = ifelse(first_cell_id %in% branch_driver, "driver",
                        ifelse(first_cell_id == 0, "truncal", "subclonal")))

cls = c("subclonal" = "gainsboro", "driver" = "forestgreen", "truncal" = "darkgoldenrod3")

p_forest = plot_forest(forest_plot, all_ids)

p_sticks = plot_sticks(
  forest = forest_plot %>% filter(cell_id %in% all_ids),
  labels = muts_plot %>% filter(first_cell_id %in% all_ids) %>%
    dplyr::select(cell_id = first_cell_id, label) %>% unique(),
  cls = cls
)

p_vaf = plot_vaf(muts_plot, vaf_cut = 0.03, colors = cls, size = 0.1, assemble = FALSE)

ggarrange(
  p_forest,
  p_sticks,
  ggarrange(plotlist = p_vaf$pairs, ncol = 3, nrow = 2, legend = "none"),
  ggarrange(plotlist = p_vaf$marginals, ncol = 2, nrow = 2, legend = "none"),
  nrow = 2, ncol = 2
)
```

## From the data to the model input

The model input is built from the population sizes of the "-" and "+"
compartments at the two sampling times, the number of mutations on the
driver branch, and the CCF of the driver in the four sorted samples.
Population sizes and mutation counts are perturbed with measurement noise.

```{r prepare-data}
```

The prior on the driver "+" → "-" switch rate is derived from the data:

```{r driver-prior}
```

```{r}
omega_gamma
```

The tables required by `init_multirates()`:

```{r tables}
```

```{r}
tables
```

## Inference

`fit_multirates()` samples the posterior with Hamiltonian Monte Carlo
(NUTS) via cmdstanr: here 4 chains with 1000 warmup and 5000 sampling
iterations each. Convergence is assessed in
`vignette("Convergence_diagnostics")`.

```{r fit, results = "hide"}
```

Posterior summary, next to the values used to simulate the data:

```{r}
x$inference$multirates$summary(variables = names(truth)) %>%
  mutate(truth = truth[variable]) %>%
  dplyr::select(variable, truth, mean, median, sd, q5, q95, rhat, ess_bulk)
```

## Prior vs posterior

Prior (transparent) and posterior (solid) distributions; dashed lines mark
the values used to simulate the data.

```{r, fig.width=8, fig.height=6}
x = get_posterior_multirates(x)

plot_prior_posterior(x, params = names(truth), truth = truth)
```

## Posterior predictive checks

`get_predicted_trajectories()` simulates new data from the posterior along a
time grid. For every draw, the latent "-" and "+" sizes of each population
are computed from the model; each population then gets a lognormal total
count and a beta "+"/"-" split, as in the likelihood, and CCFs are evaluated
on the sampled counts within the "-" and "+" samples. Observed data are
shown in red.

```{r}
pred = get_predicted_trajectories(x)
```

Fraction of "+" cells in the whole population and total population size:

```{r, fig.width=10, fig.height=3.5}
ggarrange(plot_fractions(x, pred), plot_counts(x, pred), ncol = 2)
```

Fraction of "+" cells within each population:

```{r, fig.width=8, fig.height=3.5}
plot_split(x, pred)
```

CCF of each population in the "-" and "+" samples:

```{r, fig.width=8, fig.height=3.5}
plot_ccf(x, epistate = "-", pred = pred)
```

```{r, fig.width=8, fig.height=3.5}
plot_ccf(x, epistate = "+", pred = pred)
```
